Disaster preparedness handbook · earthquake & tsunami guidance

contacts.name: National emergency hotline
contacts.description: For emergencies anywhere in the Philippines.

steps.title: Move early to higher ground
steps.text: Follow evacuation instructions before access is cut off. Avoid floodwater and water-covered roads or bridges.

steps.title: Ask for a safe evacuation destination
steps.text: Contact BDRRMO or your barangay for the currently open evacuation center and safe route. This page does not track shelter capacity or road conditions.

steps.title: Take care when returning
steps.text: Do not use flood-exposed electrical systems or appliances until a qualified electrician has checked them. Avoid food or drinking water contaminated by flooding.

steps.title: Get outside immediately
steps.text: Warn others, leave belongings behind, and use stairs instead of elevators. Do not return inside.

steps.title: Avoid smoke and blocked exits
steps.text: Stay low if you must pass through smoke. Use another escape route if a door is hot or your way out is blocked.

steps.title: Call from a safe place
steps.text: Call 161, 911, or the Bacoor fire station. Tell responders if anyone is still inside. If trapped, keep the door closed, call for help, and signal from a window.

steps.title: Duck, cover, and hold
steps.text: If indoors, shelter under a sturdy table and hold on. Stay away from glass and heavy objects that could fall.

steps.title: Keep clear of falling hazards
steps.text: If outside, move to an open area away from buildings, walls, posts, and power lines.

steps.title: After shaking stops
steps.text: Exit calmly using stairs when safe. Expect aftershocks and keep away from damaged buildings.

situations.label: Typhoon & storm surge
situations.title: Prepare before the storm reaches you

steps.title: Follow weather and local advisories
steps.text: Read PAGASA bulletins and local evacuation instructions. Conditions at the coast can change as a typhoon approaches.

steps.title: Plan a route to higher ground
steps.text: Coastal storm surge can rapidly flood low-lying areas. Identify a safe destination with your barangay before an evacuation is needed.

steps.title: Leave when advised
steps.text: Follow local evacuation orders and take your emergency supplies. Ask BDRRMO which evacuation center is open; a mapped building is not proof that it is operating.

steps.title: Move away from the coast
steps.text: After a strong coastal earthquake, or sudden unusual sea-level changes, move immediately to higher ground.

steps.title: Do not approach the shoreline
steps.text: Do not go to the beach to watch or investigate receding water.

steps.title: Wait for the official all-clear
steps.text: A tsunami can involve several waves. Stay away from danger areas until authorities allow return.

steps.title: Call 911 or Bacoor’s 161
steps.text: Ask for emergency medical assistance. For Red Cross ambulance assistance, call 143.

steps.title: Explain where help is needed
steps.text: Give your location and nearby landmark, explain what happened, and answer the dispatcher’s questions.

steps.title: Follow the dispatcher’s instructions
steps.text: BetterBacoor cannot dispatch an ambulance or assess an injury. The responding service will advise on availability and next steps.

situations.label: Police & immediate danger
situations.title: Get help for an immediate threat

steps.title: Call for urgent assistance
steps.text: Use 161, 911, or the published Bacoor police number for an immediate threat or police emergency.

steps.title: Tell the responder what is happening
steps.text: Give the incident’s location and follow the responder’s instructions. This website does not receive emergency reports.
